question: to the Commission Mathilde Androuët (PfE) Subject:

In its communication COM(2021)592 final of 29 September 2021 on the application of Directive 2009/52/EC on sanctions against employers, the Commission promoted access for irregular immigrants to complaint, aid and reporting mechanisms, including via third parties (NGOs, trade unions, associations). Whilst the fight against employers operating outside the law is essential to combat exploitation and social dumping, the effective enforcement of removal decisions is an equally essential element in ensuring the credibility of the European Union’s migration policies. In view of the above: 1.

What precise amounts, broken down by Member State and by EU financial instrument, have been allocated since 2021 to actions directly or indirectly benefitting irregular immigrants under these mechanisms?
Which measures ensure that this funding does not, in practice, contribute to keeping persons subject to a return decision on Member State territory?
Does the Commission intend to make this funding conditional on verifiable results in terms of recovered penalties and effective cooperation with supervisory and return authorities?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.6.2026) Funding under the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF)1 is mainly implemented under shared management. Information on EU spending under shared management is available on the Cohesion Open data Platform2. In May 2026, the Commission launched a EUR 10 million call for expression of interest3 for the specific action4 ‘Protecting thirdcountry workers’ rights while fighting against illegal employment of irregularly staying thirdcountry nationals. Under direct management, in 2024, the Commission launched a call for proposals on assistance, support and integration of third country national victims of trafficking in human beings5 for a value of EUR 6 million. This call also aimed to support the prevention of labour exploitation of third-country nationals as well as the awareness on the risks of labour exploitation. Member States must ensure that any actions implemented with the support of the AMIF programmes is compliant with the relevant EU acquis, including EU rules on returning illegally staying third-country nationals. The Commission regularly monitors the implementation of the Employer Sanctions Directive6 by Member States and organises regular expert group meetings on the topic of irregular migration and the Directive to exchange information and good practices. The latest implementation report was adopted in May 20267. The conditions for AMIF funding are laid down in the AMIF Regulation, the Financial Regulation and the Common Provisions Regulation.
